strengths: Impressive and comprehensive empirical results across 8 diverse benchmarks with substantial improvements over closed-source models (+11.12%) and open-source baselines (+17.12%)
Thorough experimental evaluation including ablation studies, component analysis, OOD performance, and statistical significance testing across multiple datasets
Clear demonstration of scalability with increasing number of LLMs (Figure 4) showing consistent performance gains without apparent saturation
Practical system with competitive cost ($8.11 vs $15.36) and reasonable latency (12.32s) despite computational complexity
Detailed analysis of system components including retrieval patterns (Fig. 5), prior-actual performance correlation (Table 4), and diversity-quality trade-offs (Fig. 6)
Comprehensive implementation details, hyperparameter sensitivity analysis (Tables 11-13), and cost-effectiveness studies enabling reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: RPS is straightforward RAG application to question bank, scoring mechanisms are standard, and EPE exploration is conventional prior-weighted sampling; contribution is primarily engineering/systems-level rather than algorithmic innovation
Critical dependence on question bank quality and diversity without principled construction guidelines; OOD performance degradation (Table 3) raises concerns about generalization to truly novel tasks

Experimental fairness concerns: different baseline configurations (Symbolic-MoE marked with *), task-specific prompts (Fig. 8) differing from baselines, fixed aggregator selected post-hoc, and artificial 'upper bound' baseline definitions

Hybrid scoring mechanism (Eq. 7) lacks strong justification: balance coefficient λ=1.0 set without sensitivity analysis, unconventional PPL formulation (1-PPL), and Appendix A.7's handling of numerical scale mismatch is hand-wavy

Reproducibility and scalability barriers: requires deployment of 15 LLMs with pre-computation of ~5,512 questions × 15 models, code not yet released, and prohibitive resource requirements for most researchers

Insufficient theoretical justification for core design choices: why should question-level retrieval similarity predict LLM capability match? Pairwise ranking score (Eq. 8) is convoluted without clear motivation
Missing analysis of failure cases, error categorization, and qualitative examples; no investigation of optimal team composition or which models complement each other best
Limited ablation on critical hyperparameters: tolerance coefficient γ=0.95, N_sup_base=400, K=7, n=8 choices lack justification; sensitivity analysis missing for different task types

strengths: Well-motivated problem formulation with clear identification of scalability limitations in existing multi-LLM systems
Clever retrieval-based prior selection design that avoids complex preprocessing while enabling adaptive, instance-level LLM selection
Comprehensive empirical evaluation across 8 diverse benchmarks with strong consistent improvements over both closed-source (GPT-4.1, GPT-o3-mini) and open-source baselines
Excellent experimental rigor: thorough ablations, OOD generalization tests, statistical analysis, aggregator selection studies, cost-efficiency curves, and component contribution analysis
Clear scalability demonstration showing monotonic performance improvement with increasing number of LLMs (Fig. 4)
Practical feasibility with competitive cost ($8.11) and latency compared to proprietary models
Well-executed system design combining retrieval-based selection with exploration-exploitation-driven enhancement
Clear presentation with helpful visualizations and generally well-organized writing
weaknesses: Evaluation setup concern: unified question bank constructed from benchmark validation sets, creating potential distribution alignment bias toward test performance; baseline comparisons with prior work (Symbolic-MoE, MoA) may not use identical 15-LLM pools

Limited algorithmic novelty: RPS is essentially standard RAG applied to LLM selection; EPE combines existing techniques (perplexity, similarity, dropping); contribution is primarily system design rather than novel algorithms
Hyperparameter choices lack principled justification: K=7, n=8, λ=1.0, γ=0.95, etc. appear empirically tuned; fixed aggregator (Llama-3.3-70B) is task-dependent yet treated as universal

Perplexity scoring methodology: combining S_sim ∈ [0,1] with S_PPL ∈ [-∞,0] with λ=1.0 treats mismatched scales; assumption that perplexity (predictability) correlates with answer correctness is insufficiently justified; no learning of λ
Suspicious uniformity of improvements across all 8 benchmarks with no failure mode analysis, suggesting possible evaluation bias or overfitting to benchmark distributions
Reproducibility gaps: code not released (only promised); multiple LLM versions and embeddings complicate reproduction; unclear if task-specific prompts were tuned independently
Loose 'exploration-exploitation' framing: not formulated as formal multi-armed bandit problem; exploration phase is simply random dropping based on prior scores
Limited scalability demonstration: only shown up to 15 models; question bank may become bottleneck with many more LLMs; unclear if improvements persist to 50+models
Incomplete baselines: no comparison with recent routing methods despite citing RouterDC and GraphRouter; missing simple baselines like random or equal weighting

Generalization concerns: all evaluation on standardized benchmarks with objective answers; no evaluation on open-ended generation, real-world queries, or user studies; applicability to subjective correctness is unclear
